question.leadin: Give the following about the decolonization of Africa.
question.text: This former French colony's National Liberation Front, or FLN, won its independence in an eight-year war that ended with the Evian Accords.
question.clue: Ahmed Ben Bella served as the first president of this country after a war that led to many pieds-noirs ("p'yay-NWAR") fleeing this country.

swap.text: Not to be accused of lacking attention to detail, Amin also clarified that he was the conqueror of this country "in Particular". Idi Amin brutally ruled this country for most of the 1970s, during which he expelled all Asians from it.
swap.clue: The issuance of the Common Man's Charter in this country was part of a socialist doctrine called the Move to the Left, which also involved taking control of sixty percent of eighty corporations after the Nakivubo Pronouncement.

question.leadin: This city was the target of the Jameson Raid, which was instead stopped at Doornkop.
question.text: Name this capital of Gauteng province, the most populous city in South Africa.
question.clue: The Jameson Raid was an attempt to take over this largest city in South Africa.

swap.text: This African nation, which also suffers from hyperinflation, is led by Robert Mugabe. To "counter" inflation, this nation removed 10 zeros from its currency in 2008, making 10 billion dollars equal to one.
swap.clue: It's not Kenya, but British intervention in this country led to the Lancaster House agreement that ended Ian Smith's white minority rule.

question.leadin: One city in this empire included a massive library of Islamic learning at the University of Sankore ["sahn-CORE-eh"].
question.text: Name this empire, the home of many griots that recorded oral history. One griot epic tells the story of Sundiata Keita founding this empire by beating Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.
question.clue: That founder defeated the Sosso monarch Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.

swap.text: This Emperor of Ethiopia was overthrown during the Italian occupation. Despite a moving address to the League of Nations, he was forced to remain in exile until the end of World War II.
swap.clue: He was eventually deposed, in part because of a famine in the Wollo region, by a committee known as the Derg.

question.text: The Derg fought a war over the Ogaden ("OH-gah-den") region with this country, at the time led by Siad Barre ("see-AHD BAR-reh"). In 1993, the US launched Operation Gothic Serpent to capture Mohamed Farrah Aidid ("eye-DEED") in this country.
question.clue: After the dictator Siad Barre was ousted from power in this nation, warlords began to take control of autonomous regions such as Puntland.

swap.text: The system for effective removal of shipwrecks from national waters was determined at a convention in Nairobi, the capital of this African country.
swap.clue: The Kapenguria Six were arrested during a conflict in this modern-day country, which also saw the British construct "protected villages" to detain civilians.

question.text: This son of Nandi and Senzangakona forged the Zulu empire through military innovations like the buffalo horns formation and the iklwa spear, which replaced the assegai.
question.clue: The iklwa was a shortened version of the assegai promoted by this commander, who was succeeded by Dingane after his assassination.

swap.text: The Almoravids were based in Marrakesh, a city in this modern-day country. This country was also the home of the Almohads and various other Berber tribes.
swap.clue: An English colony in this country , inherited through Charles II's marriage into the House of Braganza, was blown up after its parliamentary funding was withdrawn.

question.text: Much of the unhappiness of Mozambique was centered in this city, the nation's capital.

swap.leadin: Thomas Sankara's efforts to preserve this region in Burkina Faso included planting 10 million trees and restricting random logging.
swap.text: The Great Green Wall initiative seeks to prevent the desertification of what region by planting trees from Senegal to Djibouti?
swap.clue: This semiarid region south of the Sahara stretches from the Atlantic Ocean to the Red Sea.

question.leadin: This polity fought against a colonial power in battles at Mbumbi and Mbwila.
question.text: Identify this kingdom that was founded by a "nami" named Lukeni lua Nami. It had its capital at Mbanza.
question.clue: Civil wars in this empire include one between the rival Kinlaza and Kimpanzu dynasties, as well as one against the rebellious Counts of Soyo.

swap.text: This city was the nominal capital of Ethiopia during the civil war that followed Tewodros II's assassination. This Ethiopian city was founded by Fasilides, who built a gigantic bath in it.
swap.clue: Iyoas I was murdered in this city, which was built to control trade routes by the emperor Fasilides.

question.leadin: In the late 1940s this colony was the site of the "groundnut scheme," in which Britain's Labour government wasted at least 36 million pounds.
question.text: Name this African territory, which became a Class B mandate under the League of Nations in 1922.
question.answerHtml: Tanganyika [prompt on Tanzania; do not accept or prompt on “Zanzibar”]
question.clue: This colony that became a country of the same name before uniting with Zanzibar to its east. Its name means "sail in the wilderness" in Swahili, referencing a lake of the same name on its western border.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about European diplomacy in the first decade of the 20th century FTPE.
swap.text: This 1906 conference confirmed the independence of Morocco and gave France the authority to control Morocco's Algerian border.
swap.clue: The First Moroccan Crisis between France at Germany was defused at this 1906 conference. Britain honored the Entente Cordiale here by backing the French side completely.

question.leadin: The Gao Kinglist records fourteen kings from this dynasty, including Kusoy, who converted to Islam in 1010 CE, and its mythical first ruler who came from Yemen and settled at the town of Kukiya.
question.text: Name this early dynasty, from which Sunni Ali and the Songhai people descended. An indigenous people of western Niger is still named for being descended from this Dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Za Dynasty [or Zuwa Dynasty] (the Zarna are the people meaning “descended from the Za”)

swap.text: This founder of the National Union of Popular Forces, a leftist party in Morocco, disappeared in Paris in 1965. Ronen Bergman's 2018 book Rise and Kill First alleges that he was killed in a Mossad safe house by Moroccan intelligence operatives and French police officers.

question.text: This institution first perpetuated the Tutsi-dominant beliefs of Leon-Paul Classe, then supported the Bahutu Manifesto's call for an end to Hutu discrimination. This institution abetted the massacre, then bulldozing, of 20,000 civilians in Nyarubuye during the Genocide.
question.answerHtml: Roman Catholic Church in Rwanda [prompt on Christian Church]

swap.leadin: He is the author of the noted religious text The Gospel According to the Ghetto.
swap.text: Name this man who united the ZANU and ZAPU parties before his downfall in an ugly sodomy scandal.
swap.clue: This man preceded Mugabe as President of Zimbabwe and is known for forming the Zimbabwe African National Union. He was also sentenced to 10 years in jail for sodomy in 1999.
